# Palo Alto Extraction Remediation Plan

This implementation plan covers the complete remediation of the Palo Alto source parser to use the canonical `ExtractionResult` accounting rather than best-effort "XML -> IR". It enforces the "zero silent loss" principle and addresses known unsafe semantic fallback behaviors (such as inventing `any` or `allow`).

## User Review Required

> [!WARNING]
> This is a major overhaul of the Palo Alto source parser (`src/fwmigrate/parsers/palo_alto/parser.py`) and its integration points.
> It introduces `ExtractionResult` context and stops treating canonical IR as the *only* source representation.
> Please review the order of execution below to ensure it aligns with your expectations.

## Open Questions

> [!NOTE]
> 1. Are there any specific test coverage targets (e.g. branch coverage %) required for the newly added `tests/` files, or should we just ensure all listed use cases have at least one test case?
> 2. Should `palo_alto/objects.py` only be extracted from `parser.py` if `parser.py` becomes too large, or do you prefer starting with them separated? (The plan assumes keeping them in `parser.py` initially and splitting only if necessary).

## Proposed Changes

The work will be executed in 19 distinct phases, exactly as outlined in your instructions:

---

### Phase 0: Add Safety Regression Baseline
Freeze the current behavior and add failing tests for dangerous semantic issues before refactoring.

## Verification Plan

### Automated Tests
- Run `pytest tests/ -v` to ensure all existing and newly added regression/safety tests pass.
- Verify that test phases 01-16 fail or pass appropriately as development progresses, culminating in a 100% green test suite in phase 19.

### Manual Verification
- Review the `Extraction Coverage` and `Source Configuration` sheets in the generated Excel exports to ensure all raw XML rules and context have been preserved.
- Inspect the CLI execution outputs to confirm malformed inputs flag `PARSE_ERROR`.
